correctness.rationale: The equilibrium equations split exhaustively into \(x=0\) and \(x\ne0\). The first gives the three real roots of \(F(y)=0\) with free \(z\); the second forces \(z=0\), \(x=-a_6y/a_7\), and a quadratic with negative constant term, hence exactly two nonzero real roots. Independent symbolic reconstruction gives \(\det(\lambda I-J)=\lambda(\lambda^2+a_5zF'(r))\) on every line. Since \(F'(0)<0\) and \(F'(r_\pm)>0\), the stated zero-Hopf and saddle-normal half-lines follow exactly.
correctness.risk: The theorem is linear-spectral at nonisolated equilibria and does not establish nonlinear center-manifold dynamics.

final_claim: For the cubic oscillator \(\dot x=F(y)+a_4x^2,\ \dot y=-a_5xz,\ \dot z=a_6xy+a_7x^2\), \(F(y)=a_1y^3-a_2y^2-a_3y\), with all \(a_i>0\), the equilibrium set consists exactly of three affine lines at \(y=0,r_+,r_-\) and two isolated points obtained from \(a_1y^2+By-a_3=0\), \(B=a_4a_6^2/a_7^2-a_2\). At a line point \((0,r,z)\), the characteristic polynomial is \(\lambda(\lambda^2+a_5zF'(r))\); consequently the zero-Hopf locus is the negative half of the zero line and the positive halves of the two nonzero lines.
limitations: No nonlinear zero-Hopf bifurcation theorem is claimed.
